sources.title: March 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.evidence_location: official HTML overview and contract table
facts: Snapshot date is 17 March 2026
Contracted premises cover initial contract scope only
Figures are not directly comparable with official statistics
Values are rounded to the nearest 10
limitations: Management information does not prove current retail orderability
Contract totals cannot be assigned to a parcel

sources.title: May 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
sources.evidence_kind: monthly contract-level management information with data-quality notice
facts: The release records reductions for two contracts after supplier data resubmissions
The reductions are described as administrative-data revisions rather than delivery-performance changes
Contracted premises cover initial scope only
The figures are not directly comparable with official statistics
limitations: Revised historical values must not be treated as physical network removal
Monthly totals cannot be assigned to a parcel

sources.title: June 2026: Premises contracted and built under Project Gigabit contracts
facts: Snapshot date is 17 June 2026
Contracted premises cover initial contract scope only
There is a variable lag between delivery and BDUK ingestion
The figures should not be used to assess contractual milestones
limitations: Built counts do not prove retail orderability

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire
facts: The redesigned contract covers around 6,000 premises
The reported public investment is £24.4 million
The redesign followed commercial-rollout expansion and market changes
The redesign aims to reduce overlap with commercial rollout
limitations: Contract scope is not completed build or live orderability
A premise may be outside scope for several stated reasons

sources.title: Project Gigabit network build contract - Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire
facts: CityFibre is no longer delivering the contract
BDUK and CityFibre mutually agreed to end the contract
The page cites wider market conditions and expanded commercial rollout
BDUK reports discussions with other suppliers for remaining premises
limitations: Contract termination does not mean all premises lack coverage
Alternative-supplier discussions are not completed delivery
